big_ideas.title: Choose the system first
big_ideas.text: Every analysis starts by drawing a boundary. What is inside fixes which forces are internal, which energies are stored, and which quantities are conserved; a system can be treated as one point at its center of mass when its insides don't matter.

big_ideas.title: Interactions are forces, and forces come from fields
big_ideas.text: Objects act on each other in pairs (contact, gravitational, electric, magnetic). The net external force sets how a system's motion changes; at a distance the interaction is carried by a field that exists whether or not a test object is there.

big_ideas.title: Conserved quantities shortcut the details
big_ideas.text: Energy, momentum, angular momentum and charge are neither created nor destroyed; they move between objects and forms. When the system is chosen so nothing crosses its boundary, before = after, no matter how messy the middle.

big_ideas.title: Change has a rate and an accumulation
big_ideas.text: Velocity, acceleration, current and power are rates; displacement, work, impulse and charge are accumulations. Slopes and areas on graphs, and derivatives and integrals in the calculus layer, move between them.

big_ideas.title: Waves carry energy and superpose
big_ideas.text: Oscillations that propagate move energy without moving matter; overlapping waves add, which produces interference, standing waves, diffraction and beats.

big_ideas.title: At small scales energy comes in packets
big_ideas.text: Light arrives as photons of energy hf, matter has a wavelength h/p, atoms have discrete energy levels, and nuclei turn mass into energy.

practices.title: Create diagrams
practices.text: Draw a diagram, table or schematic (motion diagram, free-body diagram, energy bar chart, ray diagram, circuit) that represents the situation.

practices.title: Graph data
practices.text: Plot a quantitative graph with scales and units, linearise where useful, and read slopes and intercepts.

practices.title: Sketch qualitative graphs
practices.text: Sketch the shape of a graph that a model predicts (x–t, v–t, U–x, I–t) without numbers.

practices.title: Derive an expression
practices.text: Combine laws and definitions symbolically to get the quantity asked for in terms of the givens.

practices.title: Calculate with units
practices.text: Compute or estimate a number with correct units and significant figures.

practices.title: Compare
practices.text: Compare a quantity across situations, times or locations and say which is larger and why.

practices.title: Predict from functional dependence
practices.text: Say how a quantity changes by what factor when another is changed (doubles, quarters, unchanged).

practices.title: Design an experiment
practices.text: Propose what to measure, with what, and how to reduce uncertainty to answer a question.

practices.title: Apply the right model
practices.text: Pick the law, definition or model that fits the situation and its validity limits, and use it to make a claim.

practices.title: Justify with evidence
practices.text: Support or refute a claim with physical principles, data or a representation.

topics.title: Scalars and vectors in one dimension

los.do: Classify a quantity as a scalar or a vector and state a vector's magnitude and direction.
ek: A vector has magnitude and direction (displacement, velocity, force); a scalar has magnitude only (distance, speed, mass, energy).

los.do: Add collinear vectors using a sign convention for direction.
ek: In 1-D, pick a positive direction; opposite vectors carry opposite signs and add algebraically.

los.do: Calculate displacement and distinguish it from distance travelled.
ek: Δx = x_f − x_i depends only on start and end points; distance is the total path length.

los.do: Calculate average velocity and average acceleration over a time interval.
ek: v_avg = Δx/Δt; a_avg = Δv/Δt; acceleration opposite to velocity means slowing down.

los.do: Read instantaneous velocity and acceleration from slopes, and displacement and Δv from areas, on motion graphs.
ek: Slope of x–t is v; slope of v–t is a; area under v–t is Δx; area under a–t is Δv.

los.do: Solve a constant-acceleration problem with the kinematic equations.
ek: v = v₀ + at; x = x₀ + v₀t + ½at²; v² = v₀² + 2aΔx; pick the one missing the unknown you don't need.

los.do: Analyze vertical free fall as motion with constant acceleration g downward.
ek: Near Earth's surface a = −9.8 m/s² (up positive) throughout the flight, including at the top where v = 0.

los.do: Translate between a narrative, a motion diagram and consistent x–t, v–t and a–t sketches.
ek: The three graphs must agree: where v–t crosses zero, x–t has a turning point; constant a gives a straight v–t and a parabolic x–t.

los.do: Calculate an object's velocity as measured by observers in different inertial frames moving along one line.
ek: v_A rel C = v_A rel B + v_B rel C; all inertial observers measure the same acceleration.

topics.title: Vectors and motion in two dimensions

los.do: Resolve a vector into perpendicular components and rebuild a vector from its components.
ek: A_x = A cos θ, A_y = A sin θ (θ from +x); |A| = √(A_x² + A_y²), θ = tan⁻¹(A_y/A_x) with quadrant check.

los.do: Analyze a horizontally launched projectile by treating horizontal and vertical motion independently.
ek: Ignoring air: a_x = 0, a_y = −g; the two directions share only the time.

los.do: Calculate time of flight, maximum height and range of a projectile launched at an angle.
ek: v_y = 0 at the top; on level ground R = v₀² sin 2θ / g, maximal at 45°.

los.do: Add relative velocities in two dimensions (boat crossing a river, plane in a crosswind).
ek: Relative velocities add as vectors; add components, then find magnitude and heading.

los.do: Choose a system and sort the forces on it into internal and external.
ek: Internal forces cancel in pairs; only external forces change the motion of the system's center of mass.

los.do: Calculate the center of mass of a system of point masses.
ek: x_cm = Σm_i x_i / Σm_i (each axis separately); it lies closer to the heavier parts.

los.do: Identify each force on an object as an interaction with a named other object, contact or at a distance.
ek: Every force has an agent; no agent, no force ("force of motion" is not a force).

los.do: Draw a free-body diagram with every force on the object, from its point of action, in the correct direction.
ek: Normal force is perpendicular to the surface, tension along the string away from the object, gravity toward Earth's center.

los.do: Identify third-law force pairs and distinguish them from balanced forces on one object.
ek: A third-law pair is equal and opposite, acts on two different objects and is the same type of force.

los.do: Find an unknown force (tension, normal, applied) on an object in translational equilibrium.
ek: Constant velocity (including rest) ⇔ ΣF = 0; write ΣF_x = 0 and ΣF_y = 0 separately.

los.do: Apply ΣF = ma to one object to find its acceleration or an unknown force.
ek: a = ΣF/m points along the net force; the kinematics then follows from Unit 1.

los.do: Find the acceleration and string tension of connected objects (Atwood machine, blocks joined by a string).
ek: Treat the whole as one system for a, then isolate one object for the tension; an ideal string has one tension and one |a|.

los.do: Analyze an object on an incline by resolving gravity along and perpendicular to the surface.
ek: Along the incline mg sin θ, into it mg cos θ; on a frictionless incline a = g sin θ.

los.do: Calculate the gravitational force between two masses with Newton's law of gravitation.
ek: F = Gm₁m₂/r², r center to center; doubling r quarters F.

los.do: Calculate the gravitational field strength g at a planet's surface or at altitude.
ek: g = GM/r²; weight mg is the gravitational force, and g is also the free-fall acceleration.

los.do: Calculate kinetic friction on a sliding object and the acceleration it produces.
ek: f_k = μ_k N, opposite to the relative sliding velocity; N is found from the perpendicular force balance, not assumed to be mg.

los.do: Decide whether static friction can hold an object and find the friction force actually acting.
ek: f_s ≤ μ_s N: static friction is whatever the balance needs, up to the maximum; slipping starts when the need exceeds μ_s N.

los.do: Apply Hooke's law to find a spring force, stretch or spring constant, including k from a force–extension graph.
ek: F_s = −kΔx, restoring toward equilibrium; k is the slope of F vs Δx.

los.do: Calculate centripetal acceleration and identify which real force supplies the net inward force.
ek: a_c = v²/r toward the center; centripetal is a role (tension, friction, gravity, normal), never an extra force on the FBD.

los.do: Apply ΣF_r = mv²/r to a car on a flat curve, a vertical loop or a conical pendulum.
ek: Flat curve: μ_s mg ≥ mv²/r; top of a loop: N + mg = mv²/r, minimum speed √(gr).

los.do: Derive the speed and period of a circular orbit from gravity as the centripetal force.
ek: GMm/r² = mv²/r ⇒ v = √(GM/r), T² = 4π²r³/(GM); orbital speed is independent of the satellite's mass.

los.do: Calculate translational kinetic energy and predict how it scales with speed and mass.
ek: K = ½mv² is a scalar, never negative; doubling v quadruples K.

los.do: Calculate the work done by a constant force over a straight displacement.
ek: W = Fd cos θ; a force perpendicular to the motion (normal, centripetal) does no work; friction on a sliding object does negative work.

los.do: Find work as the area under a force–position graph, including the work to stretch a spring.
ek: W = area under F–x; for a spring from 0 to x, W = ½kx².

los.do: Apply the work–energy theorem to find a speed or a force.
ek: W_net = ΔK; the net work is the sum of the work done by each force.

los.do: Calculate gravitational potential energy near Earth and elastic potential energy of a spring for a system.
ek: U_g = mgh (reference level is a choice; only ΔU matters); U_s = ½kx²; potential energy belongs to a system of interacting objects.

los.do: Calculate the gravitational potential energy of two widely separated masses.
ek: U_G = −Gm₁m₂/r with U = 0 at infinite separation; it rises toward zero as r grows.

los.do: Apply conservation of mechanical energy to find a speed, height or spring compression.
ek: With only conservative forces doing work inside the system, K_i + U_i = K_f + U_f.

los.do: Account for friction and external work in an energy balance.
ek: ΔK + ΔU + ΔE_th = W_ext; sliding friction converts f_k d into thermal energy.

los.do: Calculate the escape speed from a planet's surface.
ek: ½mv_esc² − GMm/R = 0 ⇒ v_esc = √(2GM/R), √2 times the circular orbital speed at the same r.

los.do: Calculate average power and the instantaneous power delivered by a force.
ek: P_avg = W/Δt = ΔE/Δt; P = Fv cos θ; 1 W = 1 J/s.

los.do: Calculate the momentum of an object and of a system, and relate system momentum to the center-of-mass velocity.
ek: p = mv is a vector; p_sys = Σm_i v_i = M v_cm.

los.do: Calculate impulse as average force times time or as the area under F–t, and equate it to the change in momentum.
ek: J = F_avg Δt = Δp; the same Δp over a longer time needs a smaller force (airbags, bent knees).

los.do: Apply conservation of momentum in one dimension, including explosions and recoil.
ek: If the net external impulse on the system is zero, p_sys before = p_sys after; an explosion from rest gives m₁v₁ = −m₂v₂.

los.do: Apply conservation of momentum in two dimensions by components.
ek: Momentum is conserved separately along x and along y.

los.do: Classify a collision as elastic or inelastic by comparing kinetic energy before and after.
ek: Momentum is conserved in every isolated collision; kinetic energy only in elastic ones.

los.do: Find the final velocity and the kinetic energy lost in a perfectly inelastic collision.
ek: Objects stick: v_f = (m₁v₁ + m₂v₂)/(m₁ + m₂); the lost K becomes thermal energy and deformation.

los.do: Find both final velocities in a one-dimensional elastic collision.
ek: Conserve p and K; equivalently the relative speed reverses: v₁ − v₂ = −(v₁′ − v₂′).

los.do: Solve a two-stage problem (ballistic pendulum) with momentum for the collision and energy afterward.
ek: Energy is not conserved through the inelastic collision, momentum is not conserved during the swing; use each only where it holds.

los.do: Solve constant-angular-acceleration problems with the rotational kinematic equations.
ek: ω = ω₀ + αt; θ = ω₀t + ½αt²; ω² = ω₀² + 2αΔθ — the linear equations with θ, ω, α.

los.do: Convert between angular and linear quantities for a point on a rotating object.
ek: s = rθ, v = rω, a_t = rα (θ in radians); every point shares ω, speed grows with r.

los.do: Calculate the torque of a force about an axis and its sense of rotation.
ek: τ = rF sin θ = r⊥F (lever arm); counterclockwise positive by convention.

los.do: Calculate the rotational inertia of point masses and combine given inertias of rigid shapes.
ek: I = Σm_i r_i²; inertias about the same axis add; mass far from the axis costs the most.

los.do: Shift a rotational inertia to a parallel axis.
ek: I = I_cm + Md²; I is smallest about an axis through the center of mass.

los.do: Find unknown forces on a beam, ladder or sign in static equilibrium.
ek: ΣF = 0 and Στ = 0 about any axis; choose the axis through an unknown force to drop it.

topics.title: Newton's second law in rotational form

los.do: Apply Στ = Iα to find the angular acceleration of a rigid object.
ek: α = Στ/I about a fixed axis or the center of mass.

los.do: Solve a massive-pulley problem by coupling the translational and rotational equations.
ek: Each hanging mass: ΣF = ma; pulley: (T₁ − T₂)R = Iα; no-slip: a = Rα. Tensions differ when the pulley has mass.

units.title: Energy and momentum of rotating systems

los.do: Calculate the rotational kinetic energy of a rigid object.
ek: K_rot = ½Iω².

los.do: Calculate the work done by a torque and apply the rotational work–energy theorem.
ek: W = τΔθ for constant τ; W_net = ΔK_rot.

los.do: Calculate the angular momentum of a rigid object and of a point mass moving past an axis.
ek: L = Iω for a rigid object; L = mvr⊥ for a point mass (r⊥ = perpendicular distance from the axis to the line of motion).

los.do: Relate angular impulse to the change in angular momentum.
ek: τ_avg Δt = ΔL; area under τ–t is ΔL.

los.do: Apply conservation of angular momentum to a spinning skater, a merry-go-round or a mass striking a rod.
ek: Zero net external torque ⇒ I_iω_i = I_fω_f; K_rot can change (it rises when I drops).

los.do: Find the speed of an object rolling without slipping down an incline, and rank shapes by speed.
ek: v = Rω; K = ½Mv² + ½Iω²; with I = βMR², v = √(2gh/(1 + β)) — smaller β wins.

los.do: Compare a satellite's speed at different points of an elliptical orbit using angular momentum and energy.
ek: Gravity exerts no torque about the planet: mv_1r_1 = mv_2r_2 at perigee and apogee; total K + U_G is constant.

los.do: Calculate the kinetic, potential and total energy of a circular orbit.
ek: K = GMm/2r, U = −GMm/r, E = −GMm/2r; a lower orbit is faster but has less total energy.

los.do: Identify simple harmonic motion from a restoring force proportional to displacement and locate the equilibrium position.
ek: SHM ⇔ F = −kx about equilibrium; a vertical spring oscillates about its stretched equilibrium, not its natural length.

los.do: Calculate the period and frequency of a mass on a spring.
ek: T = 2π√(m/k), f = 1/T, ω = 2πf; independent of amplitude.

los.do: Calculate the period of a simple pendulum at small amplitude.
ek: T = 2π√(L/g), independent of mass; valid for small angles.

los.do: Write x(t) for an oscillator from a graph or a description, and say where speed and acceleration are largest.
ek: x = A cos(2πft + φ); |v| is maximum at equilibrium, |a| maximum at the turning points.

los.do: Apply energy conservation to an oscillator to find speed at a position or the maximum speed.
ek: ½kA² = ½mv² + ½kx² ⇒ v_max = A√(k/m) = Aω.

los.do: Calculate density and use it to compare materials or find a mass or volume.
ek: ρ = m/V; water is 1000 kg/m³.

los.do: Calculate pressure from force and area, and convert between absolute and gauge pressure.
ek: P = F⊥/A; P_abs = P_gauge + P_atm, P_atm ≈ 1.01 × 10⁵ Pa.

los.do: Calculate the pressure at a depth in a static fluid.
ek: P = P₀ + ρgh; depends on depth only, not on the container's shape.

los.do: Calculate the buoyant force on an object and decide whether it floats, and how deep.
ek: F_b = ρ_fluid V_displaced g (Archimedes); a floating object displaces its own weight, fraction submerged = ρ_obj/ρ_fluid.

los.do: Calculate the force multiplication of a hydraulic lift.
ek: Pascal: a pressure change spreads undiminished, F₁/A₁ = F₂/A₂ (work in = work out).

los.do: Apply the continuity equation to find a flow speed or volume flow rate.
ek: Incompressible flow: A₁v₁ = A₂v₂ = volume flow rate; narrower pipe ⇒ faster flow.

los.do: Apply Bernoulli's equation to find a pressure or speed, including efflux from a tank.
ek: P + ½ρv² + ρgy is constant along a streamline (energy per volume); open tank drain v = √(2gh).

topics.title: Kinetic theory of temperature and pressure

los.do: Explain gas pressure as momentum delivered by molecular collisions and predict how it changes with speed and number density.
ek: Each wall collision transfers 2mv_x; more molecules per volume or faster molecules ⇒ higher pressure.

los.do: Relate absolute temperature to average molecular kinetic energy and calculate an rms speed.
ek: K_avg = (3/2)k_B T; v_rms = √(3k_BT/m); at the same T lighter molecules move faster.

los.do: Apply the ideal gas law to find an unknown state variable or the change between two states.
ek: PV = nRT = Nk_BT with T in kelvin; for a fixed amount P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂.

los.do: Predict the direction of heat transfer between objects in contact and the condition for thermal equilibrium.
ek: Heat flows spontaneously from higher to lower T until temperatures are equal (zeroth law).

los.do: Calculate the internal energy of a monatomic ideal gas and its change.
ek: U = (3/2)nRT for a monatomic ideal gas; ΔU depends only on ΔT.

los.do: Calculate the work done on a gas from the area under a P–V curve, and identify isobaric, isochoric, isothermal and adiabatic paths.
ek: W_on = −∫P dV = −(area under P–V) for expansion; isobaric W = −PΔV, isochoric W = 0.

los.do: Apply the first law to find Q, W or ΔU for each type of process.
ek: ΔU = Q + W (W on the gas); isothermal ΔU = 0, adiabatic Q = 0, isochoric W = 0.

los.do: Analyze a cyclic process on a P–V diagram for net work and net heat.
ek: Over a cycle ΔU = 0, so Q_net = −W_net = enclosed area (clockwise = net work done by the gas).

los.do: Calculate the heat needed for a temperature change and the final temperature of a calorimetry mixture.
ek: Q = mcΔT; in an insulated mixture ΣQ = 0, so heat lost by the hot = heat gained by the cold.

los.do: Calculate the rate of heat conduction through a slab.
ek: Q/Δt = kAΔT/L; thicker or less conductive ⇒ slower.

los.do: Predict whether the entropy of a system and its surroundings increases, decreases or stays the same in a process.
ek: The total entropy of an isolated system never decreases; spontaneous heat flow and mixing raise it.

los.do: Calculate the efficiency of a heat engine and compare it with the Carnot limit.
ek: e = W/Q_H = 1 − Q_C/Q_H ≤ 1 − T_C/T_H (kelvin); bridge to engineering thermodynamics — check against the current CED.

los.do: Calculate the electric force between two point charges with Coulomb's law.
ek: F = k|q₁q₂|/r², k = 8.99 × 10⁹ N·m²/C²; like charges repel, unlike attract.

los.do: Find the equilibrium of a charged object acted on by both electric and gravitational forces.
ek: Electric force dwarfs gravity between particles; for a hanging charged ball, tan θ = F_e/(mg).

los.do: Account for the permittivity of a medium in electric force calculations.
ek: k = 1/(4πε), ε = κε₀; a medium with κ > 1 weakens the force by a factor κ.

los.do: Find the net electric force on a charge from several others by vector superposition.
ek: Each pair force is computed independently; add the vectors by components.

los.do: Track charge through charging by friction, conduction and induction, including sharing between identical conductors.
ek: Charge is conserved and quantized (e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C); identical touching spheres end with equal shares.

los.do: Calculate the electric field of one or more point charges.
ek: E = kq/r², away from + and toward −; fields from several charges add as vectors.

los.do: Calculate the force on a charge in a field and its resulting motion in a uniform field.
ek: F = qE, a = qE/m; a charge entering a uniform field moves like a projectile.

los.do: Describe the field of charged conductors and the uniform field between oppositely charged parallel plates.
ek: In electrostatic equilibrium E = 0 inside a conductor and E is perpendicular to its surface; between large plates E is uniform.

los.do: Sketch and interpret electric field lines.
ek: Lines start on +, end on −, never cross; their density shows field strength.

los.do: Calculate the electric potential energy of a system of point charges.
ek: U = kq₁q₂/r for each pair (sign included), U = 0 at infinity; total = sum over pairs.

los.do: Calculate the electric potential at a point due to point charges.
ek: V = kq/r, a scalar: add with signs, no components; U = qV.

los.do: Relate potential difference to a uniform field, and sketch equipotentials.
ek: |E| = ΔV/d, pointing toward lower V; equipotentials are perpendicular to field lines.

los.do: Calculate the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor and the charge it stores.
ek: C = κε₀A/d; Q = CΔV.

los.do: Calculate the energy stored in a capacitor.
ek: U_C = ½QΔV = ½C(ΔV)² = Q²/(2C).

los.do: Find the speed of a charge accelerated through a potential difference.
ek: ΔK = −qΔV; 1 eV = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ J is the energy an electron gains across 1 V.

los.do: Calculate current as the rate of charge flow and state its conventional direction.
ek: I = ΔQ/Δt (1 A = 1 C/s); conventional current runs from + to − outside the source.

los.do: Calculate the resistance of a wire from its resistivity and dimensions.
ek: R = ρL/A; longer or thinner ⇒ larger R.

los.do: Apply Ohm's law to find a current, voltage or resistance.
ek: ΔV = IR for an ohmic element (linear I–V graph, slope 1/R).

los.do: Calculate the power dissipated by a resistor and rank bulb brightness.
ek: P = IΔV = I²R = (ΔV)²/R; brightness follows power.

los.do: Calculate the equivalent resistance of series and parallel combinations.
ek: Series R_eq = ΣR (same I); parallel 1/R_eq = Σ1/R (same ΔV); parallel R_eq is less than the smallest branch.

los.do: Calculate the equivalent capacitance of series and parallel combinations.
ek: Parallel C_eq = ΣC; series 1/C_eq = Σ1/C — the reverse of resistors.

los.do: Find the terminal voltage of a battery with internal resistance.
ek: ΔV_terminal = ε − Ir; equals ε only when no current flows.

los.do: Apply the loop rule to find an unknown voltage or current in a single loop.
ek: ΣΔV = 0 around any closed loop (energy conservation); +ε across a source − to +, −IR going with the current.

los.do: Apply the junction rule to find an unknown branch current.
ek: ΣI_in = ΣI_out at a junction (charge conservation).

los.do: Solve a multi-loop circuit with the loop and junction rules together.
ek: Assign branch currents, write one junction equation fewer than junctions and enough loop equations; a negative answer means the guessed direction was wrong.

los.do: Find the currents in an RC circuit just after the switch closes and after a long time.
ek: An uncharged capacitor acts as a wire at t = 0; a fully charged one carries no current (open branch).

los.do: Calculate the time constant of an RC circuit and sketch charge and current versus time.
ek: τ = RC; charging Q rises toward CΔV and I decays toward 0, ~63% of the change per τ.

los.do: Sketch the magnetic field of a bar magnet or of Earth and describe magnetic dipoles.
ek: Field lines leave N and enter S and form closed loops; there are no isolated magnetic poles.

los.do: Calculate the magnetic force on a moving charge and find its direction with the right-hand rule.
ek: F = |q|vB sin θ, perpendicular to both v and B (reverse for negative charge); it does no work.

los.do: Calculate the radius and period of a charged particle's circular path in a uniform magnetic field.
ek: qvB = mv²/r ⇒ r = mv/(qB); period 2πm/(qB) is independent of speed.

los.do: Find the speed a velocity selector passes undeflected.
ek: Crossed fields balance when qE = qvB ⇒ v = E/B.

los.do: Calculate the magnetic field near a long straight wire and give its direction.
ek: B = μ₀I/(2πr), circling the wire (right-hand grip rule); μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T·m/A.

los.do: Calculate the force on a current-carrying wire in a field, including between two parallel wires.
ek: F = ILB sin θ; parallel currents attract, antiparallel repel.

los.do: Calculate the magnetic flux through a loop.
ek: Φ_B = BA cos θ, θ between B and the loop's normal; unit weber (T·m²).

los.do: Apply Faraday's law to find the average induced emf from a change in flux.
ek: |ε| = N|ΔΦ_B/Δt|; flux can change through B, area or angle.

los.do: Determine the direction of an induced current with Lenz's law.
ek: The induced current makes a field that opposes the change in flux, not the flux itself.

los.do: Calculate the motional emf, current and magnetic force for a rod sliding on rails.
ek: ε = BLv; I = ε/R; the force ILB on the rod opposes its motion.

los.do: Apply the law of reflection and locate the image in a plane mirror.
ek: θ_i = θ_r from the normal; a plane-mirror image is virtual, upright, same size, as far behind as the object is in front.

los.do: Draw a ray diagram to locate the image formed by a concave or convex mirror.
ek: Principal rays: parallel → through F, through F → parallel, through C → back on itself; convex mirrors always give virtual, upright, reduced images.

los.do: Apply the mirror equation and magnification to find image position, size and orientation.
ek: 1/f = 1/s_o + 1/s_i, f = R/2; M = −s_i/s_o; real images have s_i > 0 and are inverted.

los.do: Calculate an index of refraction and apply Snell's law at an interface.
ek: n = c/v; n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂; light bends toward the normal entering a higher-n medium.

los.do: Calculate the critical angle and decide whether total internal reflection occurs.
ek: sin θ_c = n₂/n₁, only for light going from higher to lower n.

los.do: Draw a ray diagram to locate the image formed by a converging or diverging lens.
ek: Parallel ray → through far F (converging) or away from near F (diverging); ray through the center goes straight.

los.do: Apply the thin-lens equation and magnification and classify the image.
ek: 1/f = 1/s_o + 1/s_i (f < 0 diverging); M = −s_i/s_o; an object inside f of a converging lens gives a virtual magnified image.

topics.title: Properties of wave pulses and waves

los.do: Classify a wave as transverse or longitudinal and describe what it carries.
ek: A wave transports energy, not matter; transverse = medium moves ⟂ to propagation, longitudinal = ∥ (sound).

los.do: Apply v = fλ to find a wavelength, frequency or speed.
ek: v = fλ = λ/T; the medium sets v, the source sets f.

los.do: Calculate the wave speed on a stretched string.
ek: v = √(F_T/μ), μ = mass per length.

los.do: Predict the reflected and transmitted pulses at a boundary between media.
ek: Reflection off a fixed end (or a denser medium) inverts the pulse; frequency is unchanged on crossing, speed and wavelength change.

los.do: Calculate the intensity of light transmitted through polarizers.
ek: Only transverse waves polarize; unpolarized → I₀/2, then I = I₀cos²θ through each later polarizer.

los.do: Place radiation in the electromagnetic spectrum and calculate its frequency or wavelength.
ek: All EM waves travel at c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m/s in vacuum, c = fλ; in a medium v = c/n and λ shrinks.

los.do: Predict and calculate the observed frequency shift when a sound source or observer moves.
ek: Approach ⇒ higher f, recede ⇒ lower; f′ = f(v ± v_o)/(v ∓ v_s).

los.do: Apply superposition to decide whether two waves interfere constructively or destructively at a point.
ek: In-phase sources: path difference mλ ⇒ constructive, (m + ½)λ ⇒ destructive.

los.do: Find the harmonic frequencies of a string or an air column open or closed at one end.
ek: String or open pipe λ_n = 2L/n (all n); closed pipe λ_n = 4L/n (odd n only); f_n = v/λ_n.

los.do: Calculate the beat frequency of two nearby tones.
ek: f_beat = |f₁ − f₂|.

los.do: Predict how much a wave spreads through an opening and locate single-slit minima.
ek: Spreading is large when λ is comparable to the slit width a; dark fringes at a sin θ = mλ (m ≠ 0).

los.do: Locate bright fringes for a double slit or grating and calculate fringe spacing.
ek: Bright: d sin θ = mλ; small angles Δy = λL/d; a grating gives sharper, brighter maxima.

los.do: Find the film thickness that gives constructive or destructive reflection.
ek: Reflection off a higher-n layer adds a half-wave shift; count shifts, then 2nt = mλ or (m + ½)λ accordingly.

los.do: Calculate the energy of a photon from its frequency or wavelength.
ek: E = hf = hc/λ; hc ≈ 1240 eV·nm.

los.do: Calculate the de Broglie wavelength of a moving particle.
ek: λ = h/p; wave behavior shows when λ is comparable to the size of what it meets.

topics.title: The Bohr model of atomic structure

los.do: Use the Bohr model to give the energy levels of hydrogen.
ek: E_n = −13.6 eV/n²; electrons occupy only discrete levels; ionization from n is |E_n|.

los.do: Calculate the wavelength of light emitted or absorbed in a transition between levels.
ek: hf = |E_upper − E_lower|; an atom absorbs only photons that match a level difference.

los.do: Find the peak wavelength of blackbody emission from the temperature, or the reverse.
ek: Wien: λ_max T = 2.898 × 10⁻³ m·K; hotter objects peak at shorter λ.

los.do: Calculate the total power radiated by a hot surface.
ek: P = εσAT⁴ with T in kelvin; doubling T multiplies P by 16.

los.do: Calculate the maximum kinetic energy or stopping potential of photoelectrons and the threshold frequency.
ek: K_max = hf − φ = eV_stop; below f₀ = φ/h no electrons at any intensity.

los.do: Calculate the wavelength shift of a photon scattered by an electron.
ek: Photons carry p = h/λ; Δλ = (h/m_ec)(1 − cos θ) from momentum and energy conservation.

los.do: Calculate the energy released in a nuclear reaction from the mass defect.
ek: E = Δmc², 1 u ↔ 931.5 MeV; fission of heavy and fusion of light nuclei both move toward higher binding energy per nucleon.

los.do: Write a balanced alpha, beta or gamma decay equation.
ek: Nucleon number A and charge Z are conserved; α removes ⁴₂He, β⁻ turns n → p + e⁻ + ν̄, γ changes neither.

los.do: Calculate the amount remaining or the elapsed time from a half-life.
ek: N = N₀(½)^(t/T½); decay is random per nucleus but predictable in bulk.

topics.title: Displacement, velocity and acceleration as derivatives

los.do: Differentiate a position function to get velocity and acceleration as functions of time.
ek: v = dx/dt, a = dv/dt = d²x/dt²; turning points where v = 0.

los.do: Integrate a time-dependent acceleration or velocity with initial conditions to get v(t) and x(t).
ek: v(t) = v₀ + ∫₀ᵗ a dt′, x(t) = x₀ + ∫₀ᵗ v dt′; the constant-a equations are the special case.

los.do: Find velocity as a function of position when acceleration depends on position or velocity.
ek: a = v dv/dx ⇒ ∫v dv = ∫a(x) dx; for a(v), separate dt = dv/a(v).

topics.title: Motion in two or three dimensions

los.do: Differentiate and integrate a vector position r(t) component by component.
ek: r = x î + y ĵ + z k̂; v = dr/dt and a = dv/dt act on each component independently.

topics.title: Center of mass of continuous objects

los.do: Calculate the center of mass of a rod or plate with nonuniform density by integration.
ek: x_cm = ∫x dm / ∫dm with dm = λ(x) dx (or σ dA); uniform symmetric objects have it at the geometric center.

topics.title: Newton's second law with time-varying forces

los.do: Find v(t) and x(t) for an object under a time-dependent net force.
ek: ΣF = dp/dt = m dv/dt for constant m; integrate F(t)/m for v(t).

los.do: Set up and solve the equation of motion for a falling object with linear drag, and find its terminal velocity.
ek: m dv/dt = mg − bv ⇒ v(t) = v_T(1 − e^(−t/τ)), v_T = mg/b, τ = m/b.

los.do: Resolve the acceleration of an object in nonuniform circular motion into tangential and radial parts.
ek: a_t = dv/dt, a_r = v²/r; |a| = √(a_t² + a_r²).

los.do: Calculate the work done by a position-dependent force by integration.
ek: W = ∫F · dr = ∫F_x dx in 1-D; the spring's ½kx² is ∫kx dx.

los.do: Derive the potential energy function of a conservative force.
ek: ΔU = −∫F dx; gravity between masses gives U = −GMm/r with U(∞) = 0.

los.do: Find the force from a potential energy function and locate and classify equilibria on a U(x) graph.
ek: F_x = −dU/dx; equilibrium where dU/dx = 0, stable at a minimum, unstable at a maximum; turning points where U = E.

los.do: Calculate instantaneous power as a derivative and the work delivered by a time-varying power.
ek: P = dW/dt = F · v; W = ∫P dt.

los.do: Calculate the impulse of a time-varying force by integration and the resulting velocity.
ek: J = ∫F dt = Δp; F = dp/dt.

los.do: Differentiate and integrate θ(t), ω(t) and α(t) for nonconstant angular acceleration.
ek: ω = dθ/dt, α = dω/dt; integrate with initial conditions as in linear kinematics.

los.do: Compute torque as the cross product r × F from components.
ek: τ = r × F, |τ| = rF sin θ, direction by the right-hand rule along the rotation axis.

los.do: Derive the rotational inertia of a rod, ring or disk by integration.
ek: I = ∫r² dm; rod about center ML²/12, about end ML²/3, disk ½MR², ring MR².

units.title: Angular momentum and rolling with calculus

los.do: Compute angular momentum as r × p and apply τ_net = dL/dt.
ek: L = r × p for a particle, Iω for a rigid body about a symmetry axis; net torque is the rate of change of L.

los.do: Find the acceleration and the static friction force for an object rolling without slipping down an incline.
ek: Ma = Mg sin θ − f, fR = Iα, a = Rα ⇒ a = g sin θ/(1 + I/MR²); rolling friction does no work.

los.do: Derive the SHM differential equation from Newton's second law and read the angular frequency off it.
ek: F = −kx ⇒ d²x/dt² = −(k/m)x; any system of the form ẍ = −ω²x oscillates with ω.

los.do: Solve for amplitude and phase from initial position and velocity.
ek: x = A cos(ωt + φ); A = √(x₀² + (v₀/ω)²), tan φ = −v₀/(ωx₀).

los.do: Derive the small-angle period of a physical pendulum from the rotational equation of motion.
ek: −mgd sin θ = Iθ̈, sin θ ≈ θ ⇒ T = 2π√(I/(mgd)); a point mass on a string gives back 2π√(L/g).

los.do: Calculate the electric field of a continuous charge distribution (rod, ring, arc) by integration.
ek: dE = k dq/r², dq = λ dl; integrate components and use symmetry to cancel some.

los.do: Calculate the electric flux through a flat or closed surface.
ek: Φ_E = ∫E · dA; uniform field through a flat area Φ = EA cos θ; field lines through a closed surface count net enclosed charge.

los.do: Apply Gauss's law to find the field of a spherical, cylindrical or planar charge distribution.
ek: ∮E · dA = Q_enc/ε₀; choose a surface where E is constant and parallel or perpendicular to dA.

los.do: Find the field inside a sphere or cylinder with radially varying charge density.
ek: Q_enc = ∫ρ(r) dV with dV = 4πr²dr (sphere) or 2πrL dr (cylinder).

topics.title: Electric potential from fields and distributions

los.do: Calculate a potential difference by integrating the electric field along a path.
ek: ΔV = −∫E · dr; path-independent because the electrostatic field is conservative.

los.do: Calculate the potential of a continuous charge distribution by integration.
ek: V = ∫k dq/r — a scalar integral, easier than the field.

los.do: Find the electric field from a potential function.
ek: E_x = −∂V/∂x (each component); E points down the steepest potential slope.

los.do: Find induced charges and fields for a charge inside or near a conducting shell.
ek: E = 0 in the conductor ⇒ a Gaussian surface in the metal encloses zero net charge; excess charge sits on surfaces.

los.do: Calculate how charge divides between connected conducting spheres.
ek: Connected conductors reach equal potential: kQ₁/R₁ = kQ₂/R₂ ⇒ Q ∝ R; total charge conserved.

los.do: Derive the capacitance of a parallel-plate, spherical or cylindrical capacitor.
ek: Find E by Gauss, ΔV = ∫E dr, then C = Q/ΔV; cylindrical C = 2πε₀L/ln(b/a).

los.do: Calculate the energy stored in a field from its energy density.
ek: u = ½ε₀E²; U = ∫u dV, which reproduces ½CV² for a capacitor.

los.do: Predict how inserting a dielectric changes C, Q, V, E and U with the battery connected or disconnected.
ek: C = κC₀; connected: V fixed, Q and U rise by κ; isolated: Q fixed, V, E and U fall by κ.

topics.title: Current as a rate and drift velocity

los.do: Calculate current from a charge function and relate it to drift velocity.
ek: I = dQ/dt; I = nqAv_d with n carriers per volume.

los.do: Derive and solve the differential equation for a charging or discharging RC circuit.
ek: ε − IR − q/C = 0, I = dq/dt ⇒ q(t) = Cε(1 − e^(−t/RC)); discharge q = Q₀e^(−t/RC).

los.do: Calculate the time to reach a given charge or current fraction, and the energy dissipated in the resistor.
ek: t = τ ln(1/(1 − f)) charging; total heat on discharge = initial ½CV².

topics.title: Magnetic force as a cross product

los.do: Compute the magnetic force on a moving charge or current element as a cross product.
ek: F = qv × B; dF = I dl × B, integrated along a wire.

los.do: Apply the Biot–Savart law to find B at the center of a loop or arc, or on a loop's axis.
ek: dB = (μ₀/4π) I dl × r̂ / r²; center of a loop B = μ₀I/(2R).

los.do: Apply Ampère's law to find B of a long wire (inside and out), a solenoid or a toroid.
ek: ∮B · dl = μ₀I_enc; solenoid B = μ₀nI inside, ~0 outside.

topics.title: Magnetic flux of a nonuniform field

los.do: Calculate the magnetic flux through a loop in a nonuniform field (such as near a long wire) by integration.
ek: Φ_B = ∫B · dA; next to a wire, strips dA = L dr give Φ = (μ₀IL/2π) ln(b/a).

los.do: Calculate the instantaneous emf from a time-varying flux, including a rotating coil (generator).
ek: ε = −N dΦ_B/dt; coil rotating at ω: ε = NBAω sin ωt.

los.do: Solve for the velocity of a rod on rails slowed or driven by its induced current.
ek: Retarding force B²L²v/R ⇒ m dv/dt = −(B²L²/R)v, exponential decay; with a driving force it reaches a terminal speed.

los.do: Calculate the self-inductance of a solenoid, the emf across an inductor and its stored energy.
ek: ε_L = −L dI/dt; solenoid L = μ₀N²A/ℓ; U = ½LI².

los.do: Derive and solve the current in an LR circuit after a switch closes or opens.
ek: ε − IR − L dI/dt = 0 ⇒ I = (ε/R)(1 − e^(−t/τ)), τ = L/R; an inductor resists sudden change in current.

los.do: Show that an LC circuit oscillates and find its frequency and the energy exchange between C and L.
ek: L d²q/dt² + q/C = 0 ⇒ ω = 1/√(LC) — the mass–spring equation with L ↔ m, 1/C ↔ k.
